run_metadata.coverage_summary: Severely degraded run. The environment's network egress policy blocked ALL WebFetch requests (every destination, including tender portals and even example.com, returned EGRESS_BLOCKED / an organization egress denial). Only the WebSearch tool was available. WebSearch can surface portal URLs and some opportunity titles, but it does NOT allow opening tender detail pages, so no live portal querying, pagination, or deliverables/requirements extraction was possible this run. Tier 1 (AusTender, buy.nsw, Buying for Victoria, QTenders/supply.qld, Tenders WA, and the SA/TAS/NT/ACT portals) could not be queried live. Tier 2 (water corporations, GBEs, universities/TAFE, health) and Tier 3 (SAP Ariba Discovery, BHP/Rio Tinto/Fortescue/Woodside, retail, banking) were attempted via WebSearch only. The single concrete opportunity lead that surfaced (a Hume Motorway litter & debris collection contract) was found to be ALREADY KNOWN from prior runs (dedup_key buy.nsw:tfnsw-litter-debris-collection-south-region-hume-motorway), and the search snippet mis-attributed its buyer (Transport for NSW, not Insurance and Care NSW), reinforcing that unverified snippet data must not be recorded as fact. No new, independently verifiable, buyer-originated opportunities could be confirmed without detail-page access, and per the no-fabrication rule none were invented. All portals re-observed this run were already in the known-source set, so no genuinely new source could be confirmed.
gaps: CRITICAL / infrastructure: WebFetch is entirely unavailable this run. Every WebFetch call returned EGRESS_BLOCKED (an organization egress-policy denial per /root/.ccr/README.md, which instructs to report rather than route around it). Confirmed blocked hosts include www.tenders.gov.au, www.tenders.nsw.gov.au, www.vendorpanel.com.au, and even example.com, so this is a blanket outbound-HTTP block, not a per-site issue. The routine cannot perform its core function (open detail pages, follow feeds/APIs, extract deliverables) until the environment's network policy permits outbound access to tender-portal domains.

Tier 1 government portals (AusTender, buy.nsw/NSW eTendering, Buying for Victoria, QTenders + supply.qld.gov.au, Tenders WA, Tenders SA, Tenders TAS, NT QTOL, ACT Tenders) could not be queried live or paginated. Only generic descriptions and stale/aggregator snippets were returned by WebSearch; no current RFT rows with verified IDs, publish/closing dates, or buyers could be captured.

Tier 2 (Sydney Water, Melbourne Water, SA Water EOIs; universities/TAFE; local government via VendorPanel) surfaced only via paid-aggregator snippets (australiantenders.com.au, globaltenders.com, tendersontime.com) or generic portal pages; currency, IDs and dates could not be verified, so nothing was recorded as a confirmed opportunity.

Tier 3 (mandatory): SAP Ariba Discovery / SAP Business Network Discovery has no public directory reachable via WebSearch, and its postings plus the BHP/Rio Tinto/Fortescue/Woodside portals are registration- or login-gated; with WebFetch blocked and no authenticated session, no corporate opportunity could be read. These remain portal-registration sources only (already in the known-source set); none were fabricated.

Aggregator noise: a large share of WebSearch results pointed to paid reseller/aggregator sites, which the spec forbids relying on as a source of truth; they were used only as discovery signals and not recorded as opportunities or sources.

Source discovery: no genuinely new buyer-originated source could be confirmed this run — every portal that surfaced (water corporations, Rio Tinto Buy Local, TAFE NSW, Federation University, SAP Ariba Discovery, supply.qld.gov.au/Local Buy) is already present in the known-source set.
recommended_seed_additions: Operational fix required: allow-list Australian tender-portal domains for WebFetch in this environment's network egress policy (at minimum the Tier 1 *.gov.au portals, vendorpanel.com.au, and major buyer/e-sourcing hosts), or run this routine in an environment with unrestricted outbound HTTPS, otherwise daily runs will continue to be non-functional for opportunity capture.
